title: Akoma Ntoso Version 1.0 (OASIS Standard), Part 1: XML Vocabulary; Part 2: Specifications
publisher: OASIS Open (LegalDocumentML TC)
claim_supported: A stable, standardised XML vocabulary exists for parliamentary, legislative and judicial documents, including explicit amendment/modification elements; adopted in CDAI as an expression-level representation, not as an authority.
limitations: A vocabulary, not a semantics of legal validity; conformance does not entail correctness of the marked-up content; Greek-language and Greek-instrument profiles are not defined by the standard itself.
verification: Fetched OASIS standard page 2026-08-26; approval date and part list confirmed.

title: LegalRuleML Core Specification Version 1.0 (OASIS Standard)
publisher: OASIS Open (LegalRuleML TC)
claim_supported: A standardised representation exists for deontic operators (obligation, permission, prohibition, right), defeasibility, rule superiority, temporal management of rules, and the constitutive/prescriptive norm distinction. Supports CDAI's separation of constitutive from regulative norms and its defeasible rule representation.
limitations: Provides mark-up and a rule model, not a decision procedure; conflict resolution semantics are delegated to the chosen defeasible logic; no reasoner is normative.
verification: OASIS standard announcement and specification index consulted 2026-08-26.

title: Council conclusions inviting the introduction of the European Legislation Identifier (ELI) (2012/C 325/02)
publisher: Council of the European Union / Official Journal of the European Union C 325
claim_supported: ELI establishes URI templates, a metadata model and an exchange format for legislation, adopted voluntarily by Member States; used in CDAI for expression-level identity of legislative works.
limitations: Council conclusions are an invitation, not binding law; adoption is voluntary and uneven; ELI URIs are assigned by the publishing authority, so their availability for Greek instruments depends on national implementation (see RL-055).
verification: CELEX reference located via EUR-Lex 2026-08-26; developed further by 2017/C 441/05 and 2019/C 360/01.

title: Council conclusions on the introduction of the European Case Law Identifier (ECLI) and a minimum set of uniform metadata for case law (2011/C 127/01)
publisher: Council of the European Union / Official Journal of the European Union C 127
claim_supported: Case-law identity has a standard five-part form ECLI:[country]:[court]:[year]:[ordinal] with a minimum uniform metadata set; adopted in CDAI for jurisprudence identity.
limitations: Voluntary at national level; a court that does not assign ECLI leaves the Watchtower to assign a local identity, which is then a Watchtower assertion and not a source identity.
verification: OJ C 127 reference confirmed via EUR-Lex and Library of Congress Global Legal Monitor 2026-08-26.

title: ELI — European Legislation Identifier (EU Vocabularies)
publisher: Publications Office of the European Union
version: ontology distributed as OWL; version not stated on the landing page
claim_supported: The ELI ontology is published and maintained by the Publications Office as an OWL vocabulary with four pillars (identifiers, metadata, exchange format, governance).
limitations: Fetched landing page did not state ontology version number or release date; version must be read from the distributed OWL file. Recorded as a residual verification gap (see DF-024).

title: Cellar — SPARQL endpoint and Common Data Model (CDM)
publisher: Publications Office of the European Union
claim_supported: EU-level legal metadata is queryable via a public SPARQL 1.1 endpoint over an FRBR-derived Common Data Model, which also underpins the Publications Office ELI implementation. Establishes feasibility of federated retrieval of EU authority (candidate A4) and supplies a concrete external source model for CDAI's Registry.
limitations: Availability and rate limits are not contractually guaranteed to third parties; the CDM models EU publications, not the Greek legal order; a SPARQL endpoint is not an evidentiary channel (no signed container).

title: PROV-O: The PROV Ontology (W3C Recommendation)
publisher: World Wide Web Consortium (Provenance Working Group)
claim_supported: A recommendation-status vocabulary exists for entities, activities and agents, with an associated data model (PROV-DM), constraints (PROV-CONSTRAINTS) and notation (PROV-N); adopted in CDAI as the export vocabulary for lineage.
limitations: PROV describes provenance; it neither verifies it nor constrains evidentiary strength. It has no notion of authority, custody, or degradation, so it cannot serve as CDAI's internal evidence algebra.

title: The ASPIC+ framework for structured argumentation: a tutorial
publisher: Argument & Computation (Taylor & Francis / IOS Press), vol. 5, no. 1
claim_supported: Structured argumentation with strict and defeasible inference rules supports three attack forms (on premises, on defeasible inferences by undercut, and rebuttal of defeasible conclusions), with preferences resolving conflict, and satisfies the rationality postulates of closure and direct/indirect consistency when strict rules are closed under transposition. This is the adjudication semantics adopted in CDAI (D08, I-19).
limitations: Rationality postulates hold under stated conditions (notably closure of strict rules under transposition and restricted rebuttal); complexity of the induced argumentation semantics is high; the framework does not prescribe the preference ordering, which for legal meta-norms is a normative choice (DF-016).

title: An assumption-based TMS
publisher: Artificial Intelligence, vol. 28, no. 2
claim_supported: Belief can be maintained by manipulating assumption sets (environments) and labels rather than justifications alone, so that all consistent contexts are represented simultaneously, context switching is free, retraction is avoided, and minimal inconsistent environments (no-goods) prune inference. This is CDAI's label-propagation substrate (I-16, I-17).
limitations: Label size is worst-case exponential in the number of assumptions; without an explicit bound this becomes silent degradation, which C7 forbids. CDAI therefore bounds labels and introduces the LABEL-INCOMPLETE status (I-18, DF-014).

title: A formal characterisation of institutionalised power
publisher: Journal of the Interest Group in Pure and Applied Logics (IGPL), pp. 427–443
authors: Andrew J. I. Jones; Marek Sergot
claim_supported: Norm-governed institutions empower designated agents to create normative states of affairs by performing specified act types; 'A counts-as B in context C' expresses that A is sufficient to guarantee the institutional classification B. This is the formal basis of CDAI's exclusive typed powers, warrants, and the voidness of unempowered acts.
limitations: Secondary sources disagree on the volume number (3 vs 4) for the 1996 IGPL issue; the page range 427–443 and year 1996 are consistently reported. Recorded as a citation-precision gap, not a substantive one (DF-024). The formalism characterises power; it does not supply an enforcement mechanism, which CDAI must provide (D02).

title: RFC 9162: Certificate Transparency Version 2.0
publisher: IETF / RFC Editor
authors: B. Laurie; E. Messeri; R. Stradling
claim_supported: An append-only log can be realised as a Merkle tree supporting inclusion proofs and consistency proofs, where a consistency proof efficiently demonstrates that one log state is a superset of a previous state, enabling detection of log misbehaviour. Adopted for CDAI's record integrity structure (I-28).
limitations: Status is Experimental, not Standards Track — the mechanism is well-established in deployment but the RFC itself is not a standard. Merkle consistency proves append-only behaviour only relative to a witnessed head; without independent witnesses an operator can rewrite unpublished history (DF-007).
verification: Fetched RFC Editor info page 2026-08-26; status Experimental confirmed.

title: Viewstamped Replication Revisited
publisher: MIT CSAIL, Technical Report MIT-CSAIL-TR-2012-021
claim_supported: State machine replication tolerating crash faults in an asynchronous network is achievable with view changes, replica recovery and reconfiguration. Adopted as the optional high-availability topology for CDAI's record (D28).
limitations: Crash-fault tolerance only, not Byzantine; does not protect against a malicious operator (OA-5). Replication introduces a divergence hazard that must itself be specified (PO-028).

title: Changing Legal Systems: Abrogation and Annulment. Part II: Temporalised Defeasible Logic
publisher: Proceedings of NORMAS / Deontic logic workshop series
claim_supported: Abrogation and annulment are formally distinct norm-change operations with different temporal effects (ex nunc vs ex tunc), requiring two timelines — one internal to a temporal version of the legal system and one over the evolution of the system itself; belief-revision techniques are inadequate for retroactive legal change. This grounds CDAI's cessation trichotomy (R-05, I-12) and its nine-axis temporal model (R-04).
limitations: The formalism is developed for defeasible logic generally, not for Greek law specifically; mapping Greek κατάργηση / ακύρωση / ανίσχυρο onto abrogation/annulment is a legal-classification judgement the Tribunal must make per instrument, not a formal consequence.

title: Industrial hardware and software verification with ACL2
publisher: Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society A, 375(2104):20150399
authors: Warren A. Hunt Jr.; Matt Kaufmann; J Strother Moore; Anna Slobodova
claim_supported: ACL2 is an interactive theorem prover whose logic is a subset of ANSI Common Lisp, is an integrated programming and proof environment, and has seen sustained industrial use since the mid-1990s at AMD, Centaur, IBM, Intel, Kestrel, Motorola/Freescale, Oracle and Rockwell Collins. This supports CDAI's claim that the kernel needs no extraction and no re-implementation step (D20, D21), and that two independently authored kernels can be admitted by the same machinery without sharing code (I-41, I-42).
limitations: ACL2's logic is first-order, applicative and total-function oriented with a guard discipline; it does not cover CLOS, conditions, threads or side effects, so only the kernel - not the shell - can be admitted. IMPORTANT: this source does NOT support claim WC-1 or claim WC-2, both withdrawn. Coincidence of ACL2's logical semantics with host execution holds for guard-verified functions on guard-satisfying inputs; ACL2 surface forms (xargs declarations, mbe, defthm) are not ANSI CL and need a compatibility shim that is itself unverified; and agreement of arithmetic, character and string semantics between ACL2 and the host is probed by differential execution, not proved. See DF-011 and DF-048.

title: Pardinus: A Temporal Relational Model Finder (and the Alloy 6 / Electrum lineage)
publisher: Journal of Automated Reasoning
authors: Nuno Macedo; Julien Brunel; David Chemouil; Alcino Cunha
claim_supported: Alloy 6 (formerly Electrum) supports mutable relations and past and future linear temporal logic constraints, with bounded and complete model-checking backends. Adopted for CDAI's structural power-exclusivity and lifecycle obligations (PO-001, PO-003, PO-008, PO-009, PO-012, PO-023, PO-034).
limitations: Alloy analysis is bounded by scope; a property verified within scope is not proved for all sizes. The complete backend applies to specific fragments. Scope adequacy must be argued separately (DF-013).

title: TLA+ Model Checking Made Symbolic (Apalache)
publisher: Proceedings of the ACM on Programming Languages (OOPSLA)
authors: Igor Konnov; Jure Kukovec; Thanh-Hai Tran
claim_supported: TLA+ specifications can be checked symbolically by translating the transition relation to quantifier-free SMT constraints (Z3), enabling checking of inductive invariants and bounded safety properties; TLC (explicit) and TLAPS (interactive proof) complete the toolchain. Adopted for CDAI's protocol-level safety and liveness obligations.
limitations: Bounded safety unless an inductive invariant is supplied and proved; TLAPS proofs require substantial manual effort; a TLA+ model is a model, and its correspondence to the running shell is an argued refinement, not a compiled one (DF-012).

title: FoundationDB: A Distributed Unbundled Transactional Key Value Store (and Simulation and Testing documentation)
publisher: Apple / ACM SIGMOD 2021
claim_supported: By controlling actor scheduling and abstracting I/O behind shims, and by replacing all randomness with a seeded deterministic PRNG, an entire distributed cluster can be simulated deterministically in a single thread, enabling reproducible fault injection. This is the model for CDAI's requirement that the production scheduler and the simulation scheduler be the same scheduler (D14).
limitations: Determinism holds only for effects routed through the shims; any un-shimmed effect breaks replay. Simulation explores a sampled schedule space, not all schedules; it is a falsification tool, not a proof.

title: Logical Physical Clocks and Consistent Snapshots in Globally Distributed Databases (Hybrid Logical Clocks)
publisher: OPODIS 2014 / University at Buffalo Technical Report 2014-04
authors: Sandeep S. Kulkarni; Murat Demirbas; Deepak Madappa; Bharadwaj Avva; Marcelo Leone
claim_supported: A constant-space timestamp can capture causality like a logical clock while remaining within a bounded divergence of NTP physical time, enabling identification of consistent snapshots. Adopted for CDAI record stamping (I-28) so that causality never depends on wall-clock ordering (OA-3).
limitations: Divergence bound depends on the clock-synchronisation uncertainty epsilon, which is an operational property, not a guarantee; a clock jump beyond epsilon is a declared fault (F7) that must be detected, not assumed away.

title: Temporal features in SQL:2011
publisher: ACM SIGMOD Record, vol. 41, no. 3
claim_supported: SQL:2011 provides transaction time via system-versioned tables (system-time period) and valid time via application-time period tables; both were standardised in SQL:2011. This is the strongest standardised bitemporal baseline and is the reference point against which CDAI's nine-axis model is justified as necessary rather than gratuitous (D05).
limitations: Two axes only. No representation of defeasibility, of per-provision commencement, of retroactive applicability distinct from validity, or of the abrogation/annulment/correction trichotomy. Adequate for record-keeping, inadequate for the Greek legal order as characterised by L2 and L5.

title: legislation.gov.uk — Help: versions of legislation (as enacted, revised, point in time)
publisher: The National Archives (UK), on behalf of HM Government
claim_supported: A national legislation service can maintain as-enacted, revised and point-in-time versions with per-provision timelines showing the start dates of successive amended versions, at national scale. Establishes feasibility of point-in-time reconstruction (candidate A1) and supplies the practice baseline CDAI must exceed.
limitations: Point-in-time coverage begins from a cut-off date (documented as 1991 for the revised corpus) and revision is subject to an editorial backlog; the service does not model defeasible interpretation, evidentiary status, or its own blind spots. It is a publication system, not an epistemic one.

title: The Constitution of Greece (1975, as revised) — Article 26 (separation of powers), Article 42 (promulgation and publication of statutes)
publisher: Constitute Project (text of the Hellenic Constitution); official text published by the Hellenic Parliament
claim_supported: Art. 26: legislative power is exercised by Parliament and the President; executive by the President and the Government; judicial by the courts. Art. 42 §1: the President promulgates and publishes statutes passed by Parliament within one month of the vote, and may return a bill with reasons; §2: on a second passage by absolute majority the President is bound to promulgate and publish within ten days. Grounds L1 and L3.
limitations: The consulted text is the 2008 revision; the Constitution was further revised in 2019. Articles 26 and 42 are not understood to have been altered by that revision, but this was not verified against the 2019 consolidated official text in this phase — recorded as a verification residual (DF-024). The official Hellenic Parliament PDF could not be text-extracted by the available tooling.
verification: Article text fetched and quoted 2026-08-26 from Constitute Project.

title: Εθνικό Τυπογραφείο — Αναζήτηση ΦΕΚ (National Printing House — Government Gazette search)
publisher: Εθνικό Τυπογραφείο (National Printing House of the Hellenic Republic)
claim_supported: The National Printing House operates the official search and download service for issues of the Government Gazette (ΦΕΚ), which is the constitutive publication channel for Greek statutes and regulatory acts. This is the primary observation channel for CDAI's Observatory and the primary authority-bearing source in the Registry.
limitations: No documented public machine API was located in this phase; observation must be modelled as web retrieval with the associated fragility, rate limits and terms of use. Issue-level enumeration (series and sequential issue number per year) is the structural signal on which CDAI's enumeration-closure gap detector depends; its stability is an assumption (DF-020).

title: Εισαγωγικός Νόμος Αστικού Κώδικα (Introductory Law to the Greek Civil Code), Article 103
publisher: Text of the Introductory Law to the Civil Code (compiled by Lawspot)
claim_supported: A statute enters into force ten days after its publication in the Government Gazette unless it provides otherwise. Grounds L2 and the default-commencement defeasible rule in I-11.
limitations: Consulted via a secondary compiler rather than the official gazette text of the Introductory Law; the default is routinely displaced by express provisions, frequently at provision granularity, so the default is a defeasible rule and never a stored value.

title: Νόμος 3469/2006 «Εθνικό Τυπογραφείο, Εφημερίς της Κυβερνήσεως και λοιπές διατάξεις» (ΦΕΚ Α΄ 131/28.06.2006)
publisher: Hellenic Republic; codified text via Kodiko
claim_supported: The statute governing the National Printing House and the Government Gazette, including the electronic form of the Gazette, the digital signature applied to each electronic issue by an authorised officer, and the requirement that submitting bodies transmit texts under advanced electronic signature. Grounds L4.
limitations: Consulted in codified form via a commercial compiler rather than the consolidated official text; codification currency depends on the compiler. The specific article numbering for the digital-signature provision was not independently confirmed against the gazette text in this phase (DF-024).

title: Εγκύκλιος — Εκσυγχρονισμός διατάξεων σχετικά με το Εθνικό Τυπογραφείο
publisher: Υπουργείο Εσωτερικών (Hellenic Ministry of Interior)
claim_supported: Official ministerial guidance on the modernisation of the provisions concerning the National Printing House and electronic publication; corroborates the electronic-signature regime for Gazette submission and issue.
limitations: A circular is administrative guidance, not the statute; superseded in part by later amendments to Law 3469/2006.

title: Διόρθωση Σφάλματος υπαιτιότητας Εθνικού Τυπογραφείου (Correction of an error attributable to the National Printing House) — service description
publisher: Εθνικό Τυπογραφείο (National Printing House), official e-services portal
claim_supported: Correction of errors in published Gazette material is a formal statutory procedure under Law 3469/2006, Article 16 §§4 and 5, requestable by the submitting body, identified by the publication code (ΚΑΔ), and resulting in a correction published in the Gazette. Grounds L5, R-05 (correction limb), I-13 and the SOURCE-MUTATION adjudication path.
limitations: Covers corrections attributable to the Printing House; errors originating with the submitting body follow a different route (resubmission for publication). The service description does not state the retroactive legal effect of a correction, which remains a matter of legal classification for the Tribunal.
verification: Fetched and confirmed statutory basis quotation 2026-08-26: «σύμφωνα με τις διατάξεις των παρ.4 και παρ.5 του άρθρου 16 του ν.3469/2006».

title: Νόμος 4622/2019 «Επιτελικό Κράτος: οργάνωση, λειτουργία και διαφάνεια της Κυβέρνησης...» (ΦΕΚ Α΄ 133/07.08.2019), Άρθρα 65–66
publisher: Γενική Γραμματεία Νομικών και Κοινοβουλευτικών Θεμάτων (General Secretariat for Legal and Parliamentary Affairs), Hellenic Republic
claim_supported: Greek law provides for codification of legislation and law reform (Art. 65) and establishes the Central Codification Committee (Art. 66). Grounds L6 and the three-way distinction between official codification, official consolidated republication and Watchtower reconstruction (I-14).
limitations: The statute has been amended repeatedly (a codified version incorporating Law 5282/2026 was reported); article numbering and content must be re-verified against the current consolidated official text before relied upon operationally.

title: Regulation (EU) No 910/2014 on electronic identification and trust services for electronic transactions in the internal market (eIDAS)
publisher: European Parliament and Council / OJ L 257, 28.8.2014, p. 73
claim_supported: A qualified electronic time stamp enjoys the presumption of the accuracy of the date and time it indicates and of the integrity of the data to which they are bound, and is recognised in all Member States. Grounds the AUTHENTIC-SIGNED-ANCHORED tier of CDAI's evidentiary lattice (R-02).
limitations: A legal presumption, rebuttable in court; it establishes evidentiary weight, not truth of content. eIDAS has been amended (notably by Regulation (EU) 2024/1183); the cited Article 41 presumption is understood to persist but the consolidated text was not re-verified in this phase (DF-024).

title: IFLA Library Reference Model: A Conceptual Model for Bibliographic Information
publisher: International Federation of Library Associations and Institutions
authors: Pat Riva; Patrick Le Bœuf; Maja Žumer (Consolidation Editorial Group)
claim_supported: Consolidates FRBR, FRAD and FRSAD into a single model retaining the Work / Expression / Manifestation / Item distinction. Grounds CDAI's four-level identity scheme (R-03).
limitations: A bibliographic model; it has no concept of legal authority, validity, or amendment. WEMI must be used for identity only, never for authority (I-08, I-09).

title: Hallucination-Free? Assessing the Reliability of Leading AI Legal Research Tools
publisher: Journal of Empirical Legal Studies (Wiley); preprint Stanford RegLab / HAI
authors: Varun Magesh; Faiz Surani; Matthew Dahl; Mirac Suzgun; Christopher D. Manning; Daniel E. Ho
claim_supported: A preregistered evaluation of leading commercial retrieval-augmented legal research tools across 202 hand-scored legal queries found hallucination rates between 17% and 33%, against vendor claims of hallucination-free or hallucination-avoiding operation; the authors conclude providers' claims are overstated. This is the empirical ground for A9 (machine-learned components hold no institutional power) and for the disqualification of candidate A5.
limitations: Evaluates US legal research products on US law in 2024; it does not measure any Greek-law system and does not establish an error rate for the specific model configurations CDAI would use. It establishes that retrieval grounding alone is insufficient to license propositional authority — which is the claim relied on — and nothing stronger.

title: ARIES: A Transaction Recovery Method Supporting Fine-Granularity Locking and Partial Rollbacks Using Write-Ahead Logging
publisher: ACM Transactions on Database Systems, vol. 17, no. 1, pp. 94–162
authors: C. Mohan; Don Haderle; Bruce Lindsay; Hamid Pirahesh; Peter Schwarz
claim_supported: Write-ahead logging with analysis, redo and undo passes, fuzzy checkpoints and no-force/steal buffer policy yields correct recovery with fine-granularity locking. Grounds CDAI's checkpoint-and-redo recovery discipline (Failure model §3).
limitations: ARIES assumes a page-oriented storage manager and in-place update; CDAI's record is append-only and its state is derived, so only the checkpoint/redo discipline and the log-sequence-number reasoning transfer, not the undo machinery.

title: A truth maintenance system
publisher: Artificial Intelligence, vol. 12, no. 3
claim_supported: Data, their justifications and the ability to revise beliefs when assumptions change can be maintained as an explicit dependency network supporting dependency-directed backtracking. The justification-based alternative considered and rejected in favour of the assumption-based design (D08).
limitations: Maintains a single consistent context, so context switching requires retraction and re-derivation; unsuitable where the system must reason simultaneously about multiple maximal-consistent readings of a legal text, which is CDAI's normal case.

title: Conflict-free Replicated Data Types
publisher: SSS 2011 (Stabilization, Safety, and Security of Distributed Systems); INRIA Rapport de recherche 7687
authors: Marc Shapiro; Nuno Preguiça; Carlos Baquero; Marek Zawirski
claim_supported: Sufficient conditions exist under which replicas converge without synchronisation (Strong Eventual Consistency). Considered for the federated-cache candidate (A4) and for multi-node derived caches.
limitations: Convergence is not correctness: CRDT merge resolves conflicts by construction, which is precisely the wrong behaviour for legal conflict, where a conflict must be preserved and adjudicated, not merged. Rejected for any state carrying legal or epistemic content (D13).

title: Computational Metacognition
publisher: arXiv (Proceedings of the Ninth Annual Conference on Advances in Cognitive Systems)
claim_supported: Computational metacognition declaratively represents and monitors traces of cognitive activity in order to manage the performance of cognition itself; the MIDCA architecture separates a ground level (perception/action), an object level (interpretation/planning) and a meta level (introspective monitoring and metacognitive control), with transitions driven by impasses, failures and successes. Grounds CDAI's requirement that cognitive traces be first-class recorded data.
limitations: Metareasoning monitors reasoning, not world-adequacy: it can detect that reasoning is stuck, not that a specific gazette issue is missing. CDAI therefore extends the meta level with evidentially-grounded coverage propositions and the A6 triple; this extension is the architect's, not the cited work's.

title: Metareasoning: Thinking about Thinking
publisher: MIT Press
claim_supported: Establishes metareasoning as a distinct architectural level with an introduction defining the object-level / meta-level control and monitoring loop. Supports the claim that a meta-level is an architectural commitment rather than a presentation layer (C4).
limitations: An edited collection surveying approaches; it does not prescribe a single architecture and does not address institutional authority or evidence.

title: ANSI INCITS 226-1994 (formerly ANSI X3.226-1994) — Information Technology — Programming Language — Common Lisp
publisher: ANSI / INCITS (X3J13)
date: 1994; reaffirmed, most recently reported as INCITS 226-1994 (S2018)
claim_supported: Common Lisp is a formally standardised language whose standard has been stable since 1994, with CLOS, generic functions, method combination, conditions and restarts in the base standard. Grounds the portability half of D21 and the stability argument for a multi-decade institutional system.
limitations: The standard has not been revised since 1994; threads, networking, filesystem access beyond pathnames, and the metaobject protocol are outside it. Anything relying on them is implementation-specific by definition, which is why CDAI splits kernel (ANSI) from shell (SBCL-specific).

title: Common Lisp HyperSpec
publisher: LispWorks Ltd. (derived from the ANSI standard with permission of ANSI/INCITS)
claim_supported: The normative behaviour of ANSI Common Lisp operators relied upon in the Lisp-native design (generic functions, DEFINE-METHOD-COMBINATION, condition system, restarts, dynamic binding, packages) is available in an authoritative hypertext derivation of the standard.
limitations: Explicitly not the ANSI standard itself; where the two differ the ANSI document governs.

title: SBCL 2.6.7 User Manual
publisher: Steel Bank Common Lisp project
claim_supported: SBCL documents native threading (SB-THREAD) with mutexes, semaphores, waitqueues, barriers and atomic/CAS operations; a metaobject protocol package SB-MOP implementing AMOP; saving of core images; and package locking. Grounds the shell half of D21, D13 and D22.
limitations: Implementation-specific: none of these are ANSI. Behaviour may change between SBCL versions; the design must therefore pin a version and treat an SBCL upgrade as a change requiring the regression obligation (I-32).
verification: Manual fetched 2026-08-26; version string 'SBCL 2.6.7 User Manual' and the Threading and Metaobject Protocol chapters confirmed.

title: closer-mop — Closer to MOP compatibility layer
publisher: Pascal Costanza (project repository)
claim_supported: A compatibility layer rectifies absent or incorrect CLOS MOP features across implementations, including VALIDATE-SUPERCLASS behaviour for custom metaclasses; SBCL is documented as obeying the AMOP requirement that STANDARD-CLASS and FUNCALLABLE-STANDARD-CLASS be compatible metaclasses. Grounds the metaclass-based enforcement in D02 and D25.
limitations: A compatibility layer cannot supply semantics an implementation lacks; portability of a metaclass-based design is bounded by the weakest supported implementation. CDAI pins SBCL and uses closer-mop for hygiene, not for portability claims.

title: The Art of the Metaobject Protocol
publisher: MIT Press
authors: Gregor Kiczales; Jim des Rivières; Daniel G. Bobrow
claim_supported: CLOS is specified with an open implementation whose class, slot-access and generic-function invocation protocols are themselves programmable, permitting controlled meta-level extension (custom metaclasses, slot-access interception, class redefinition semantics). Grounds CDAI's use of MOP for persistence, access control and warranted class evolution (D25).
limitations: AMOP is not part of the ANSI standard; conformance varies by implementation. Meta-level programming increases the trusted computing base of the shell, which is why the kernel is kept MOP-free.

title: Condition Handling in the Lisp Language Family
publisher: Advances in Exception Handling Techniques, Springer LNCS 2022
claim_supported: The Common Lisp condition system separates the code that detects a problem from the code that decides how to recover, by exposing named restarts that a handler in an outer dynamic context may select without unwinding the signalling context. Grounds CDAI's separation of fault detection (Observatory, Authentication, kernel) from remedy policy (offices), D24.
limitations: A language mechanism, not an institutional one; restarts constrain control flow, not authority. CDAI must add the requirement that a restart selection is itself a warranted, recorded act, which the cited work does not address.

title: Common Lisp HyperSpec — Macro DEFINE-METHOD-COMBINATION; Method Selection and Combination
publisher: LispWorks Ltd. / ANSI Common Lisp
claim_supported: Standard method combination provides :before, :after and :around auxiliary methods; DEFINE-METHOD-COMBINATION's long form computes an arbitrary effective-method form from the applicable methods and their qualifiers, permitting user-defined control structure and arbitrary processing of qualifiers. This is the mechanism by which CDAI makes warrant checking and act recording language-level rather than conventional (D02).
limitations: A custom method combination applies only to generic functions declared to use it; it cannot police ordinary function calls, so it cannot carry an authority guarantee. In CDAI it is defence in depth: it fails fast at the call site with a good diagnostic. Authority is enforced at the append point by a call-path-independent admission predicate (I-46, PO-046). NOTE (R4): this entry previously described the mechanism as supported by the package facility acting as a boundary - claim WC-6, withdrawn.

title: ASDF Manual — Another System Definition Facility (including the package-inferred-system extension)
publisher: ASDF project (Common-Lisp.net)
claim_supported: ASDF defines systems, components and dependency ordering, and supports a one-package-per-file style in which package names map to system names and dependencies are deduced from DEFPACKAGE / UIOP:DEFINE-PACKAGE. Grounds CDAI's use of systems and packages as a DEPENDENCY model, and specifically the computation of each kernel's transitive load-time closure, on which the kernel-disjointness check I-42 / PO-042 is defined (D22).
limitations: ASDF enforces build-time dependency order, not runtime authority; a system boundary is not a security boundary. NOTE (R4): this entry previously stated that authority enforcement comes from the package facility plus warrant checking - claim WC-6, withdrawn. Authority enforcement comes from admission-side reconstruction in the verification kernel (I-46). What the package model genuinely supports is I-42 disjointness, and even there its faithfulness rests on kernel admissibility rather than on the graph alone (DF-049).

title: Bordeaux-Threads — portable shared-state concurrency for Common Lisp (API v2)
publisher: Stelian Ionescu (project documentation)
claim_supported: A portable interface exists for threads, mutexes, semaphores, condition variables and some atomic operations; APIv2 targets SMP hosts and no longer supports single-threaded implementations. Considered as the portable alternative to SB-THREAD in D21.
limitations: Portability is limited to the intersection of host capabilities; SBCL-specific facilities relied upon by CDAI's shell (package locks, core saving, CAS on structure slots) are outside its scope, so it is adopted only where it costs nothing.

title: bknr-datastore — MOP-based in-memory database with transactions for Common Lisp
publisher: BKNR project
claim_supported: Persistent CLOS objects can be implemented through the metaobject protocol with a metaclass marking slots persistent or transient, prohibiting slot access outside transactions, with durability by immediate transaction-log append plus periodic snapshot and restart-time replay. Demonstrates that MOP-mediated persistence with log-and-snapshot recovery is a proven Common Lisp technique, grounding D10's feasibility analysis and D25.
limitations: The prevalence model makes the live image the authority, which fails CDAI's axiom A12 and the deletability test A8, and it offers no answer to kernel-version evolution. CDAI therefore adopts the mechanism (MOP-enforced transactional slot access, log + snapshot) while inverting the authority relation.

title: SBCL Manual — Saving a Core Image (SB-EXT:SAVE-LISP-AND-DIE)
publisher: Steel Bank Common Lisp project
claim_supported: A core image preserving global state can be saved and optionally made executable with a specified toplevel; only global state survives, the stack is unwound, and on threaded platforms only one thread may remain when the image is saved. Grounds CDAI's use of images as fast-start checkpoints (never as the system of record).
limitations: Core images are explicitly not binary-compatible across runtimes, including runtimes built from the same sources at different times. An image is therefore a disposable cache by construction — which is exactly the status A12 assigns it — and can never be an archival format.

title: in-toto Attestation Framework
publisher: in-toto project (CNCF)
claim_supported: A specification exists for signed, verifiable claims about how an artifact was produced, carried in DSSE envelopes with typed predicates and subject digests, together with verification workflows. Adopted as the wire format for CDAI's derivation attestations and custody attestations.
limitations: Attestation formats establish who said what about which digest; they establish nothing about legal authority or evidentiary strength, and a signature by the Watchtower about its own derivation is self-attestation, not independent evidence.

title: SLSA Specification v1.1 — Provenance
publisher: OpenSSF / SLSA project
claim_supported: A build-provenance predicate records builder identity, build instructions, parameters, environment and dependency digests; SLSA recommends in-toto attestations as the vehicle. Adopted for attesting the identity of the kernel version that produced a derivation (I-07, I-30).
limitations: Concerns software supply chain, not legal evidence; SLSA levels describe build-integrity assurance and do not transfer to document authenticity.

title: Knowledge and common knowledge in a distributed environment
publisher: Journal of the ACM, vol. 37, no. 3, pp. 549–587
claim_supported: States of knowledge of groups of processes are useful primitives for designing and analysing distributed protocols; communication transforms the system's state of knowledge; distributed knowledge and common knowledge are distinct and have distinct attainability. Grounds CDAI's treatment of coverage and blindness as knowledge states of the institution rather than as metrics, and the A7 silence/blindness distinction.
limitations: The possible-worlds treatment yields high complexity (satisfiability with common knowledge is EXPTIME-complete), so CDAI uses the conceptual distinction and does not implement an epistemic modal reasoner.

title: The LKIF Core Ontology of Basic Legal Concepts
publisher: CEUR Workshop Proceedings Vol-321 (LOAIT 2007); ESTRELLA project
authors: Rinke Hoekstra; Joost Breuker; Marcello Di Bello; Alexander Boer
claim_supported: A reusable OWL ontology of basic legal concepts (norms, legal roles, powers, obligations, actions) exists and was designed for interchange of legal knowledge. Consulted as a candidate upper ontology for CDAI's legal vocabulary.
limitations: Not adopted as CDAI's core: LKIF-Core is an OWL description-logic ontology and cannot express defeasibility, per-provision temporal commencement, or evidentiary strength. Used, if at all, as an export alignment target only.

title: Διαύγεια (Diavgeia) — OpenData API and the transparency programme under Law 3861/2010
publisher: Hellenic Republic (Ministry of Digital Governance) / Diavgeia programme
date: programme established by Law 3861/2010; API samples accessed 2026-08-26
claim_supported: Decisions and acts of Greek public bodies are published online with a unique registration number (ΑΔΑ) under Law 3861/2010, exposed through a documented OpenData API with published client samples. Provides a second, machine-readable observation channel with its own enumeration signal (ΑΔΑ) for CDAI's gap detection.
limitations: Diavgeia publication is an administrative transparency requirement and does not substitute for Gazette publication as the constitutive act for statutes (L1); an act present in Diavgeia and absent from the Gazette has a different legal status, and conflating the two would violate I-02.

title: Άρειος Πάγος — Αναζήτηση αποφάσεων (Supreme Civil and Criminal Court of Greece — decision search)
publisher: Άρειος Πάγος (Areios Pagos), Hellenic Republic
claim_supported: The Supreme Court publishes anonymised civil and criminal decisions through an official search facility. This is the primary observation channel for domestic supreme-court jurisprudence.
limitations: Published decisions are anonymised and coverage is not guaranteed complete; there is no documented enumeration invariant equivalent to Gazette issue numbering, so coverage of this source may be permanently INDETERMINATE under A7 unless a reference-closure signal is available. This is a declared limit, not a defect to be papered over.

title: The Rocq Prover 9.0.0 Release Notes
publisher: The Rocq Prover project (formerly The Coq Proof Assistant), Inria and partners
claim_supported: The proof assistant formerly called Coq completed its renaming to Rocq at version 9.0, released 12 March 2025, with a single rocq binary and a renamed standard library, retaining backwards-compatible shims for Coq 8.20. Considered as an alternative proof platform in D20.
limitations: Rejected for the kernel: verification in Rocq would require either extraction to a different language or a re-implementation, which reintroduces a TRANSLATION seam that the ACL2 arrangement does not have. NOTE (R4): this entry previously asserted that ACL2 eliminates the model/code separation for a Common Lisp kernel - claim WC-1, withdrawn. The correct and narrower statement is that the translation seam is removed while the logic-to-execution seams remain (guard verification, ACL2 surface syntax, host conformance; DF-011, DF-048). Rocq is retained as a candidate for isolated deep proofs where ACL2's first-order logic is insufficient.

title: Akoma Ntoso Naming Convention Version 1.0
publisher: OASIS Open (LegalDocumentML TC)
claim_supported: A naming convention defines IRIs and identifiers for Akoma Ntoso works, expressions and manifestations, including date and language components. Supports CDAI's expression/manifestation identity layers (R-03).
limitations: A naming convention is not an identity authority; two publishers may mint different IRIs for the same normative unit, which is precisely why CDAI keeps norm identity separate and Registry-assigned (I-08).

title: European Legislation Identifier: use cases and implementation (including the Greek National Codification Portal)
publisher: Publications Office of the European Union / data.europa.eu
claim_supported: ELI is being implemented in Greece via the National Codification Portal, intended as the digital hub for legislation and codification and aligned with EUR-Lex and N-Lex, implementing ELI Pillar 3. Establishes that a Greek ELI identity space is emerging and that CDAI's Registry must be able to adopt externally-minted ELI identifiers without surrendering norm-identity authority.
limitations: Implementation status, coverage, stability and URI policy were not verified against a live Greek ELI endpoint in this phase. CDAI must therefore treat Greek ELI identifiers as defeasible external assertions (I-10), not as ground truth (DF-024).

title: An abstract framework for argumentation with structured arguments
publisher: Argument and Computation, vol. 1, no. 2
claim_supported: The generalised ASPIC framework from which ASPIC+ derives: arguments constructed from strict and defeasible rules over a knowledge base, with attack and defeat relations mapped onto abstract argumentation semantics. Supplies the argument-construction semantics underlying CDAI's docket reasoning.
limitations: Abstract argumentation semantics beyond grounded (preferred, stable) are computationally hard; CDAI restricts admitted semantics to grounded plus a bounded preferred check with an explicit incompleteness status (DF-014).

title: Simulation and Testing — FoundationDB documentation
publisher: Apple / FoundationDB project
claim_supported: Physical interfaces are replaced by shims and the epoll-based run loop by a time-based simulation, running multiple logical processes as concurrent actors, to conduct deterministic simulation of a whole cluster in one thread; every change is subjected to large-scale simulation before review. Operational corroboration of RL-017 and the direct model for CDAI's shell scheduler.
limitations: Documentation of one project's practice; transferability to a Common Lisp shell is an engineering claim CDAI must discharge by construction (all effects behind an injected environment object), not an inherited guarantee.

title: SBCL Manual — Threading (SB-THREAD): atomic operations, mutex support, semaphores, waitqueues, barriers
publisher: Steel Bank Common Lisp project
claim_supported: SBCL maps threads onto host OS threads and documents a CAS protocol, mutexes, semaphores, waitqueues and barriers. Grounds the region-thread concurrency model in D13 and the claim that the shell can be built without inventing synchronisation primitives.
limitations: Not ANSI; semantics are SBCL-specific and version-dependent. Any use inside the kernel would break ACL2 admissibility, so all threading is confined to the shell by construction.

title: Semantics of the PROV Data Model (PROV-SEM) and PROV-DM
publisher: World Wide Web Consortium
claim_supported: PROV-DM defines entities, activities, agents, generation, usage, derivation, attribution, association and delegation, with a companion formal semantics. Used to justify that CDAI's internal lineage model can be exported losslessly to an interoperable standard.
limitations: PROV's derivation relation is untyped with respect to fidelity: it can say y was derived from x but not that the derivation weakened evidentiary strength. CDAI's degradation lattice is therefore additional structure, exported as PROV qualified associations with custom properties.

title: EUR-Lex — ELI Register: technical information
publisher: Publications Office of the European Union / EUR-Lex
claim_supported: EUR-Lex documents the technical basis of its ELI implementation, including URI templates and metadata embedded in pages, and hosts the ELI register of national implementations.
limitations: A page fetch during this phase returned no extractable content; the claim rests on the page's documented role rather than on verified content, and is recorded as a residual verification gap (DF-024).

title: Government Gazette (Greece) — series and publication practice
publisher: Wikipedia (tertiary)
claim_supported: Background orientation only: the Government Gazette is the official journal in which laws are published and no law is valid until published there; issues are organised in series and sold and searchable through the National Printing House.
limitations: Tertiary source. Used solely for orientation; every legally operative claim in this phase rests on RL-021 (Constitution), RL-023 (ΕισΝΑΚ), RL-024/RL-026 (Law 3469/2006 and the official ET service) and not on this entry. Flagged explicitly so that no architectural decision depends on it.

title: Foundations of Assumption-based Truth Maintenance Systems: Preliminary Report
publisher: AAAI-87 Proceedings
claim_supported: A logical characterisation of ATMS labels in terms of prime implicates, establishing soundness and completeness conditions for label computation. Grounds the formal statement of CDAI's label-soundness obligations PO-015 through PO-017.
limitations: The characterisation is for propositional clausal theories; CDAI's arguments are structured trees over rules, so the correspondence is an argued encoding rather than a direct application, and PO-015..017 must be proved for CDAI's own label algorithm rather than cited.
